capabilities.domain_role: consume scoped requirements and return business evidence
supply current business authority, checkpoints, cursors and artifact identities
declare domain capability ceiling and action-specific requirements; current host proves executability
produce domain verification evidence without overstating assurance

capabilities.lifecycle: Incident -> Failure Class -> Change Proposal -> Reproducible Evaluation -> Promotion Authorization -> Action Authority -> Post-Promotion Observation -> Keep/Rollback/Retire
capabilities.domain_role: produce incidents, learning candidates, failure-class evidence, alternatives, eval/replay evidence and owner-scoped promotion proposals
rules: Domain-local learning is evidence/candidate generation, not a second controller or unrestricted production rewriter.
A candidate may mutate production only through the unique owning authority and normal action/side-effect controls.
Cross-domain/common-capability changes are promoted by UAOS; domain-specific business rules remain owned and promoted by the domain owner under UAOS requirement/action lineage.
Repeated failures are repaired at the common failure class/root abstraction and require regression evidence before closure.

capabilities.domain_role: supply fresh current_stage, next_action/blocker and business update/version data
expose stable version/hash/schema identities and ISO-8601 update timestamps for material authority

anti_duplication: Do not copy UAOS task indexes, continuation protocols, requirement registries, evolution catalogs or promotion state into domain repositories.
A domain may implement business-specific learning, evaluation and maintenance hooks, but those hooks feed the common governance contract rather than replacing it.
